[He continues: "O God Savitṛ, this has been declared to you; impel it and perform the sacrifice! Bṛhaspati is the Brahman priest (3.1.7a,b); may he protect the sacrifice, may he protect the lord of the sacrifice, may he protect me, O protector of the sacrifice! Bhūr bhuvaḥ suvaḥ oṃ, be established! 3.5.2.8. He should remain restrained in speech as long as the portion [of the ritual] has not been assigned... if he should speak much, he would cut off the sacrifice.
3.5.2.9. When he restrains his speech at each sacred bathing place (*tīrtha*), he becomes one whose deity is the ancestors (*pitṛdevatya*). He does not interrupt the sacrifice. 3.5.2.10.

After the *samiṣṭayajus* oblation has been offered, having gone out by the same way he came, he throws two wood-shavings (*śakala*) into the *āhavanīya* fire with [the mantra]: "Whatever injury has occurred to my self, Agni has restored my sight. 3.5.2.11.
By this very [method], he becomes the Brahman priest for the New and Full Moon sacrifices, the *iṣṭis*, the Four-Monthly sacrifices (*cāturmāsya*), and the Animal Sacrifice (*paśubandha*).

3.5.2.12. Where they carry the sacrificial cake around for him, there, having touched water, he gazes at it with his mind alone; thus he receives it with his mind, thus he eats it with his mind and his breath, and thus, having touched water, he touches his vital breaths with his mind.
Thus ends the fifth section.
By this very same [formula], the Brahman [priest] [addresses] the Dīkṣaṇīyā [offering]: "O Brahman, we shall proceed; O Hotṛ, praise the Gharma! 3.6.1.2.
Having recited the Divākīrtyā verse, the Brahman gives the impulse (prasauti).

3.6.1.3. Now, when he carries the *mahāvīra* vessel toward the east, the Brahman priest follows along behind it on the south side and performs his duties while standing to the south. 3.6.1.4. By this very same procedure, he becomes the Brahman for the *upasad* rites. While the *stambayajus* is being carried away from the great altar (*mahāvedi*), he remains seated to the south; likewise, he remains seated to the south of that which is being measured out. 3.6.1.5. He goes to the south of the fire as it is being led forward and remains seated to the south of the northern enclosing line (*parigraha*). He goes to the south of the two *havirdhāna* carts as they are being drawn forward.

3.6.1.6. He stands to the south of the Audumbarī post as it is being raised, and to the south of the *uparava* holes as they are about to be dug. Having placed the King (Soma) on his lap, he sits to the south while the *vaisarjana* offerings are being sacrificed. 3.6.1.7. While Agni and Soma are being led forward, he goes to the south. Before the fire is settled, he goes around the north of the *āgnīdhrīya* hearth and stands to the south.
3.6.1.8. Once the fire has been settled, they proceed toward the east.
3.6.1.9. Having handed over the King [Soma] to the Adhvaryu and having sat down to the right of the *havirdhāna* shed, he remains seated to the south of the animal dedicated to Agni and Soma.
3.6.1.10. While the *vasatīvarī* waters are being carried around, he stands to the south at the *āgnīdhra* shed; they dwell together there.

3.6.1.11. When they awaken him for the *prātaranuvāka*, he puts on the sacrificial cord (*yajñopavīta*), sips water, and taking the fire into himself with two verses, enters in this very manner... having gone by the east of the two *havirdhāna* sheds and by the west of the *āhavanīya* fire, he sits down in front of the southern *havirdhāna*. Once the *prātaranuvāka* has been commenced, he restrains his speech until the concluding formula.

3.6.1.12. When the *prātaranuvāka* has been concluded, having entered the *havirdhāna* shed by the eastern door and having gone around the north of the *dhruva* vessel, he sits to the south of the Soma being pressed behind the western [door], and he sits to the south of the cups as they are being drawn. 3.6.1.13. When, having drawn the cups, they proceed for the *bahiṣpavamāna* laud, 3.6.1.14. then, having taken hold of the *udgātṛ*s from behind, the *brahmā* offers a spoon-oblation with the verse: "O Bṛhaspati..."
3.6.2.1. “O Bṛhaspati, that which belongs to the enemy... O wonderful one! Svāhā!”—thus [he recites].
3.6.2.2. Then, having moved northward for the *bahis-pavamāna* chant...
3.6.2.3. When he says, "O Brahman, we shall chant; O Praśāstṛ," [the latter] says, "O Prastotṛ, O God Savitṛ, he has said this to you.

3.6.2.4. The Brahman mutters the *prasava* (impulsion): "Impel that, and sacrifice it; Bṛhaspati is the Brahman. Praise with long life! In the impulsion of the god Savitṛ, praise accompanied by Indra! He utters [the next part] mentally: "You are a ray; for habitation, quicken the habitation!"

3.6.2.5. After the *bahiṣpavamāna* has been chanted, having returned by the same way he came and sat down in front of the southern *havirdhāna* cart, he sits to the south of the animal for the *savanīya* offering.
3.6.2.6. Having offered its omentum and performed the ritual purification (*mārjana*), they proceed to the procession.
3.6.2.7. The procedure for the procession is well-established.

3.6.2.8. Having gone north of the two *havirdhāna* sheds, south of the *āgnīdhra*, and north of the *āgnīdhrīya* fire, and having circumambulated the *sadas* to the north, he looks at the two doors of the *sadas* while about to enter by the western door, saying: "O divine doors, do not burn me! 3.6.2.9. He gazes at the *sadas*, saying: "Homage to the *sadas*. He gazes at the sacrificer, saying: "Homage to the lord of the *sadas*. He gazes at the eyes of those who have already entered from the east, saying: "Homage to the eyes of the friends who go before. He says: "Homage to heaven! Homage to earth!"

3.6.2.10. Having gone to the west of the *audumbarī* post, he throws away a blade of grass from the southern half of the *sadas* in this very same manner. He sits down in this very same manner. Having sat down, he mutters [the following]. 3.6.2.11.
When the *pavamāna* chants have been introduced, he restrains his speech until the *paridhānīyā* verse; for the other *stotras* and *śastras*, it is until the *vaṣaṭ*-call. 3.6.2.12.
"Whenever he performs an action with a *ṛc* or a *yajus*, there he restrains his speech"—this is the common rule of reflection (*mīmāṃsā*).

3.6.2.13. By this very [method] he becomes the Brahman priest for the morning pressing, by this for the midday pressing, and by this for the third pressing. 3.6.2.14. When they proceed to the purificatory bath (avabhṛtha), he follows along on the south side; as they perform the rites, he stands on the south side. 3.6.2.15. By this very [method] he becomes the Brahman priest for the concluding offering (udayanīya).
3.6.2.16. By this [same rule], the *anūbandhya* and the *udavasāna* [are explained].

3.6.2.17. If the sacrifice should fail through a lapse in the *ṛc*, he should say, "Announce it to the *brahman*. 3.6.2.18. If [it fails] through the *yajus* or if [it fails] through the *sāman*, he should likewise say, "Announce it to the *brahman*."
3.6.2.19. If a failure should occur in the sacrifice on account of the *ṛc*, he should offer a spoonful (*sruvāhuti*) at the Āgnīdhra fire with the words, “*bhūs svāhā*.
3.6.2.20. If [a failure occurs] on account of the *yajus*, he should offer a spoonful at the Āgnīdhra fire itself with the words, “*bhuvas svāhā*.
3.6.2.21. If [a failure occurs] on account of the *sāman*, he should offer a spoonful at the Āgnīdhra fire itself with the words, “*suvaḥ svāhā*.”

3.6.2.22. Now, if the sacrifice should fall into error from any side whatsoever, [the priest] should melt clarified butter over the Gārhapatya fire while reciting, "From what unknown source has this arisen? Having purified it and having cleansed both the *sruva* and the *sruk* ladles, he should hold a fuel-stick right there, seat a Brāhmaṇa to the south, go forward facing east, place [the offering] upon grass or a bundle (*kūrca*), add a fuel-stick, and offer into the Āhavanīya fire with the mantra: "May the mind, as light, enjoy the clarified butter; may Bṛhaspati unite this unimpaired sacrifice."
"May all the gods here rejoice in this attenuation of our [sins]; Bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ svāhā!"—this is the universal expiation (sarvaprāyaścitti).
He who knows this is indeed a Brahman; therefore, one should appoint only such a person as the Brahman priest.

3.6.2.25. By this very [method] one becomes the Brahman priest for the Agniṣṭoma; by this for the Ukthya; by this for the Ṣoḍaśin; by this for the Atirātra; by this for the Āptoryāma; by this for the Vājapeya; by this for the Rājasūya; by this for the Arkāśvamedha; and by this for all sacrificial rites (yajñakratu). //15//
